# Permutation test
Run permutation test using script fix_run_permutation_cluster.R for SEO-COPD and cCOPD. The script will generate a file with the CpGs that are significant by chance. The CpGs that are significant by chance will be removed from the original results.

```{r}
SEO.COPD.emp <- read.csv(
  "../../../results/04_DM/04a_DM_SEOCOPD_vs_nonCOPD_ES/permutation/dm_SEOCOPD_results_with_cpg_permutated_pval_nBHcorr.csv",
  row.names = 1
  )%>%
  dplyr::filter(P.Value.emp < 0.05)

cCOPD.emp <- read.csv(
  "../../../results/04_DM/04b_DM_COPDcommon_vs_nonCOPD/permutation/dm_cCOPD_results_with_cpg_permutated_pval_with_SEO_DMPs.csv",
  row.names = 1
  )%>%
  dplyr::filter(P.Value.emp < 0.05)

head(cCOPD.emp)
```

# Get final CpGs
I want to keep CpGs that return an empirical p-value < 0.05, this CpGs are significant by chance. The next step is to compare which of my original significant CpGs are part of the random significant Cpgs. 

```{r}
sig.SEO.COPD <- res.SEO.COPD %>%
    dplyr::filter(adj.P.Val < 0.05)

# 9 random significant CpGs
rand.cpgs.SEO <- sig.SEO.COPD[!rownames(sig.SEO.COPD) %in% SEO.COPD.emp$CpG, ]

# non-random
non.rand.cpgs.SEO <- sig.SEO.COPD[!rownames(sig.SEO.COPD) %in% rownames(rand.cpgs.SEO), ]

non.rand.cpgs.SEO$CpG.id <- rownames(non.rand.cpgs.SEO)
non.rand.cpgs.SEO 
```

Overview of how i got the final dmp from limma to here.
- Sig SEO.COPD CpGs = 22253
- Sig empirical pval.emp < 0.05 SEO.COPD CpGs = 35838
- final non-random significant CpGs = non overlap (35838 and 22253) = 22253
  - This means that from the 23110 dmp only 9 where obtained by random chance.
- Non-random cCOPD = 676
- final.non.rand.cpgs.SEO = 22253 - 676 = 21577

The 21577 CpGs are significant differential methylated sites, corrected by inflation using permutation analysis.

# Subset by biological relevant range
- final.non.rand.cpgs.SEO = 22425
The filter I apply is the following:
- Those CpGs with logFC > 0.6 (~1.50 times higher in ex-smokers)
and mean > 0.2 and < 0.8 for both SEO and controls ex-smokers.

# Repeat for all the CpGs
The filtering I applied above is to reduce noisy CpGs with extremly low Pvalues and almost no logFC. These are significant mostly due to technical bias, I cannot coorect for batch effects due to the stremly low number of samples. 
Steps followed from all the CpGs tested (754425):
- I remove the 9 random CpGs, 676 cCOPD specific.
- Next, I filter by delta betas > 0.05, in beta values is 5 % difference in methylation, and keep betas between 0.2 and 0.8. 
- Use the remaining CpGs to make the volcano plot.
- Final number of CpGs 7947 represented in the Volcano.

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Subset betas matrix per condition
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mtx.win.betas <- as.matrix(ENmix::M2B(m.values))

# Match samples in the beta matrix with metadata
ctrl.samples <- pheno.data[pheno.data$SEO_COPD_Y_or_N == "Control_ES",]  # Samples in the control group
seo.COPD.samples <- pheno.data[pheno.data$SEO_COPD_Y_or_N == "SEO_COPD",] # Samples in the disease group

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Filter out random and cCOPD-specific CpGs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Remove random CpGs from significant results
filtered.cpgs <- res.SEO.COPD[!rownames(res.SEO.COPD) %in% rownames(rand.cpgs.SEO), ]
# Further remove cCOPD-specific CpGs
filtered.cpgs <- filtered.cpgs[!rownames(filtered.cpgs) %in% non.rand.cpgs.cCOPD$CpG.id, ]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Subset to Ctrl and COPD betas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Identify CpGs present in both results and beta value matrix
keep.cpgs <- which(rownames(filtered.cpgs) %in% rownames(win.m.values))

# Extract beta values for these CpGs
beta.matrix <- mtx.win.betas[keep.cpgs, ]

# Separate into control and COPD groups
ctrl.betas <- beta.matrix[, colnames(beta.matrix) %in% rownames(ctrl.samples)]

#copd.betas <- beta.matrix[, rownames(seo.COPD.samples)]
copd.betas <- beta.matrix[, colnames(beta.matrix) %in% rownames(seo.COPD.samples)]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Calculate mean methylation levels
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Calculate mean beta values (convert to percentages for interpretation)
# Calculate means using row names for safety
filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl <- rowMeans(ctrl.betas, na.rm = TRUE)[rownames(filtered.cpgs)]
filtered.cpgs$mean.copd <- rowMeans(copd.betas, na.rm = TRUE)[rownames(filtered.cpgs)]

# Convert to percentages
filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl.pct <- filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl * 100
filtered.cpgs$mean.copd.pct <- filtered.cpgs$mean.copd * 100

# Calculate methylation differences
filtered.cpgs$delta.mean <- filtered.cpgs$mean.copd - filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl
filtered.cpgs$delta.mean.pct <- filtered.cpgs$mean.copd.pct - filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl.pct
filtered.cpgs$abs.delta.mean <- abs(filtered.cpgs$delta.mean)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Apply final filters
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Define filtering criteria
MIN_DELTA <- 0.05      # 5% minimum methylation difference
MIN_BETA <- 0.2         # Lower bound for mean beta value
MAX_BETA <- 0.8         # Upper bound for mean beta value

# Apply filters:
# 1. Absolute methylation difference > 5%
# 2. Mean beta values between 20-80% in both groups
filtered.cpgs <- filtered.cpgs[
  filtered.cpgs$abs.delta.mean > MIN_DELTA &
  filtered.cpgs$mean.copd > MIN_BETA & filtered.cpgs$mean.copd < MAX_BETA &
  filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl > MIN_BETA & filtered.cpgs$mean.ctrl < MAX_BETA,
]


filtered.cpgs.same.direction <- filtered.cpgs %>%
    mutate(same_direction = ifelse(
      (logFC > 0 & delta.mean > 0) |
      (logFC < 0 & delta.mean < 0),
      TRUE, FALSE
    )) %>%
    dplyr::filter(same_direction == TRUE)

# View results
head( )
```

```{r}
explore_regression_results <- function(DMPs) {
  # Explore the data
  total_sig <- sum(DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  pos_sig <- sum(DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & DMPs$logFC > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  neg_sig <- sum(DMPs$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & DMPs$logFC < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  print(paste0("Total significant probes: ", total_sig)) 
  print(paste0("Significant probes with positive LogFC: ", pos_sig))
  print(paste0("Significant probes with negative LogFC: ", neg_sig))
}
#explore_regression_results(filtered.cpgs)
explore_regression_results(filtered.cpgs.same.direction)
```

```{r}
boxplot.single.cpg <- function(cpg, values, type, pheno.color.var, result.dir) {
  # Create result directory if it doesn't exist
  if (!dir.exists(result.dir)) {
    dir.create(result.dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Prepare data for the single CpG site
  plot.data <- data.frame(
    methylation = values[cpg, ],
    condition = pheno.color.var
  )
  # Define the desired order and colors
  condition_order <- c("Control_ES", "SEO_COPD")
  color_palette <- c("Control_ES" = "cadetblue", "SEO_COPD" = "darkred")
  
  # Convert condition to factor with desired order
  plot.data$condition <- factor(plot.data$condition, levels = condition_order)
  
  # Create the boxplot
  box.plot <- ggplot(
    plot.data,
    aes(x = condition, y = methylation, fill = condition)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.9,
      outlier.shape = NA,  # Hide outliers since we'll show all points
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      width = 0.6,
      lwd = 1.2,           # Make all boxplot lines thicker
      fatten = 2.5         # Specifically make the median line even thicker
    ) +
    geom_quasirandom( 
      aes(color = condition),
      dodge.width = 0.8,
      alpha = 0.9,
      size = 4,
      shape = 21,             # shape 21 = circle with fill and border
      color = "black",        # border (outline) color
      stroke = 1.2            # thickness of the outline
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Methylation Levels (", cpg, ")", sep = ""),
      x = "Sample type",
      y = paste0("methylation (", type, "-values)"),
      fill = "Condition"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_palette) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 18),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
      axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),  # show x-axis line
      axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),  # show y-axis line
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 18),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.position = "top",
      panel.grid = element_blank()   # Remove grid lines
    )
  
  # Create filename
  filename <- file.path(result.dir, paste0("boxplot_", cpg, ".svg"))
  
  # Save the plot
  ggsave(
    filename = filename,
    plot = box.plot,
    device = "svg",
    width = 5,
    height = 7,
    dpi = 300
  )
  
  return(box.plot)
}
```

# Conclusions
From this analysis I take the 116 CpGs for downstream analysis. Important to note that the adj.P.Val from the original fit are not very far from the threshold 0.05.


# Manhattan plots 

```{r}
#source("../04d_Visualization/manhattan_plot.R")
manh.plots.result.dir <- "../../../results/04_DM/permutation_cCOPD_SEOCOPD/plots/manhattan/"
dir.create(manh.plots.result.dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Filtered.results

filtered.cpgs$CpG.id <- filtered.cpgs$CpG
filtered.cpgs$CpG <- NULL

significance.cutoff <- 0.05
manh.plot <- filtered.cpgs %>%
                mutate(  
                Legend = dplyr::case_when(
                adj.P.Val > significance.cutoff ~ "Not.Significant",
                logFC < 0 ~ "Hypomethylated",
                logFC > 0 ~ "Hypermethylated",
                TRUE ~ "Not.Significant")
                )

to.manh.plot <- manh.plot %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    chr = chr %>%
      stringr::str_replace(
        pattern = "chr",
        replacement = ""
      ) %>%
      as.numeric()
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    CHR = chr,
    BP = pos,
    P = P.Value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(BP)
  )

ready.to.manh.plot <- to.manh.plot %>%
  dplyr::rename(SNP = CpG.id) %>%
  dplyr::select(BP, CHR, P, SNP)


volcanoplot.fc.filter <- function(df) {
  if (fc.cutoff > 0) {
    df %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        logFC >= log2(fc.cutoff)
      )
  } else {
    df
  }
}

y.bar.intercept <- to.manh.plot %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    as.character(Legend) != "Not.Significant"
  ) %>%
  volcanoplot.fc.filter() %>%
  dplyr::pull(P) %>%
  max() %>%
  log10() %>%
  (function(x) {x * -1})

colnames(ready.to.manh.plot) <- c("POS", "CHR", "pvalue", "SNP")

 fdr.threshold <- max(
    ready.to.manh.plot$pvalue[to.manh.plot$adj.P.Val < 0.05],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
 
# Convert chromosome to numeric (handles "chrX" etc)
ready.to.manh.plot <- ready.to.manh.plot %>%
  mutate(
    CHR = as.numeric(gsub("chr", "", CHR)), # Remove "chr" prefix
    POS = as.numeric(POS),                  # Ensure position is numeric
    pvalue = as.numeric(pvalue)             # Ensure p-values are numeric
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(CHR) & !is.na(POS) & !is.na(pvalue), # Remove NAs
    pvalue > 0 & pvalue <= 1                   # Validate p-values
  )
```

# Save image to use in AI ilustrator (from Sjors)

```{r}
# Get top 10 most significant CpGs
top10 <- ready.to.manh.plot %>%
  arrange(pvalue) %>%
  head(10)

y_max <- max(-log10(ready.to.manh.plot$pvalue), na.rm = TRUE) * 0.8  # Shortens Y-axis by 20%

manh.plot <- ggplot(
  ready.to.manh.plot,
  aes(x = POS/1e6, y = -log10(pvalue))  # Positions in Mb for cleaner scale
) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = factor(CHR %% 2)), 
    alpha = 0.9,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("blue4", "orange3")) +
# Top 10
geom_text(
    data = top10,
    aes(x = POS/1e6, y = -log10(pvalue), label = SNP),
    color = "black",
    size = 8,
    vjust = -0.5,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  # Facet by chromosome (scales adjust per chr)
  facet_grid(
    . ~ CHR,
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x",
    switch = "x"  # KEY: Moves strip labels to bottom
  ) +

  # Significance thresholds
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05),
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 0.8,
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(fdr.threshold),
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.8,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Custom theme adjustments
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),  # Remove x-axis ticks
    axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),  # Thicker Y-axis line
    axis.ticks.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.8),  # Thicker Y-axis ticks
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(), 
    panel.spacing.x = unit(0, "lines"),  # No spacing between chr panels
    legend.position = "none",  # Double-ensure no legend
    # Chromosome labels at bottom (KEY FIX)
    strip.placement = "outside",  # Ensures labels are outside plot area
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 12,
      vjust = 0,  # Positions text at the bottom of the strip
      margin = margin(t=-1, b = 1)  # Adds space below labels
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),  # Removes gray background
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)  # Adds space around plot
    ) +
  labs(
    x = "Chromosome",
    y = expression(-log[10](italic(p)-value)),
    color = "Chromosome"
  )+
  # Allow drawing elements (labels/segments) outside the plot area
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")#+
  

ggplot2::ggsave(
  "manhattan_plot_sig_non_random_cpgs_top10_labels2.svg",
  plot = manh.plot,
  path = manh.plots.result.dir,
  device = "svg", 
  dpi = 600,                 
  width = 20,
  height = 15,     
  units = "in"
)
```
